question: reach 15 is already tiny next to the 96-bar window. Is even 15 too many?
held_fixed: 255,937 parameters in every arm; only the dilations change (1,2,4 / 1,1,2 / 1,1,1)
reading:
reach 9's paired delta is positive (+0.0231) and it is NOT a level improvement. Two facts kill it as a candidate. First, it wins on two seeds of four (77102 +0.0514, 51015 +0.0968) and loses on the other two (77101 -0.1012, 91002 -0.0052), so the mean is carried by half the sample and the per-seed spread straddles zero - exactly the shape the sealed-reading rule forbids spending 2026 on. Second, the judge years were pre-registered BEFORE any arm ran, and they answer no: 2022 +12.0pp, 2023 -34.9pp, 2025 -6.7pp, one of three. reach 7 is worse on both counts (-0.0080, 1 of 3, and the widest spread of the three).

What the row does show is a variance effect, and it is the cleanest thing in it: the baseline's four seeds range +0.1289 to +0.3437 (sd 0.0812) while reach 9's range +0.1711 to +0.2425 (sd 0.0278). A shorter reach makes the net less dependent on which seed it drew. That is a property of the training procedure, not an edge, and it is worth remembering the next time a single-seed comparison is proposed: at reach 15 one seed is worth up to 0.21 of score, which is larger than most levers this laboratory has ever measured.
closes: A111-receptive-field. reach 15 stands. No walk-forward exam is spent on this.
